sources.entry: moviepy - A module for script-based movie editing with many formats, including animated GIFs.

summary.one_liner: MoviePy is a Python library for script-based video and audio editing, including cuts, concatenation, text overlays, compositing, custom effects, and reading and writing common formats such as GIF.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you load video and audio files, cut subclips, change volume, and add text clips positioned on screen. It can composite multiple clips on top of each other with transparency and concatenate clips together. Media is converted into numpy arrays so every frame or pixel can be accessed and custom effects can be written in a few lines. The final result is encoded back to formats such as mp4, webm, or gif. The README notes it is slower than calling ffmpeg directly because of data import and export overhead.
use_cases: cutting a clip from a longer video
adding title text over a video
compositing clips on top of each other
writing custom video or audio effects in Python
how_to_run: For development: clone the repo and run pip install -e .
notable: Edits video through Python code rather than a graphical interface
Converts frames and sounds into numpy arrays so per-pixel effects are easy to write
Supports compositing with transparency and non-linear editing
Reads and writes common audio and video formats including GIF
Runs on Windows, Mac, and Linux
caveats: v2.0 introduced major breaking changes; v1 is no longer maintained
Slower than using ffmpeg directly due to heavier import and export operations
Maintainers say the project is kept going by limited volunteer bandwidth
